description:

 # Enable advanced user for admin (or simple user)

summary: User picker doesn't allow to select back a user once removed unless losing focus
description:
Reproduction steps:
  - Create a user Foo
  - Go to the XWikiAdmin group and edit it to add users (or access any user picker: this step is only about obtaining a user picker) 
  - In the user picker type "Fo" and select user "Foo" that should have appeared
  - Use backspace to remove Foo 
  - Without losing the focus in the field, type again "Fo" 

Expected result:
  - the user "Foo" should be proposed again to be selected

Obtained result: 
  - the user "Foo" is not proposed anymore to be selected

Note that if the focus is lost (e.g. by clicking outside the input field) after removing the user from the picker, then it's possible to select again the user afterwards.

Step to reproduce:

 * Insert a display macro
 ** result: the macro is well added to the page
 * Insert another display macro
** expected result: there is another display macro added to the page
** current result: there is another macro added to the page+content of the entity page copied to the page
Therefore it is are like 3 pages included in the page.
 
Tested also on a old XWiki version, is it expected?

label: Duplicate
summary: xredirect parameter can be used for phishing
description:
The xredirect parameter is not verified and can be used to trick users to trust links to unsafe sites.

For example a link https://xwiki-instance.com/bin/login/XWiki/XWikiLogin?xredirect=//www.badboy.com/&vm=commentsinline.vm&loginLink=1
will show the correct XWiki login screen and after successful login the user will be redirected to the bad site.

This could be used in phishing mails to trick users into trusting a site.

Ideally XWiki would check  url.trustedDomains from xwiki.properties for valid redirection targets.

label: Duplicate
summary: Reset password and forgot username features are not working for subwiki users
description:
Reproduction steps:
  - Create a subwiki with "local and global users" (or local users only)
  - Create a user on that subwiki with an email address
  - Go to the login page of the wiki and click on "forgot password"
  - Insert the username of the user and submit the form

Expected result:
  - a mail is sent to perform the reset password operation

Obtained result:
  - no mail is sent at all

Note that the process works if  the entered user is a main wiki user even accessed from subwiki. The root cause of the bug is that the form is accessed using this kind of URL:
{{http://localhost:8080/xwiki/authenticate/reset}} which doesn't provide any information about the subwiki.

label: Duplicate
summary: "Preformatted names" strategy thinks single letter words are not valid
description:
The {{SlugEntityNameValidation}} aka "Preformatted names" page naming strategy thinks that several single letters (at least three) connected by hyphens do not form a valid page name, despite of generating such names itself.

To reproduce, activate that page naming strategy in the wiki admin, and set  both "Transform names automatically" and "Validate names before saving" to "Enabled".

Then try to create a page with name "a b c". An error message appears that this is not a valid page name.

summary: The 'Edit' popover button should be enhanced for short titled entries in a Live Data table
description:
STEPS TO REPRODUCE
 # Go to Sandbox.WebHome
 # Create a child page with a very short name (e.g. A)
 # On Sandbox page, click on 'More Actions' > 'Children'
 # Hover the mouse over the short titled page and observe the appearance of the 'Edit' popover button

EXPECTED RESULTS

The 'Edit' popover button is displayed right below the (short) entry name (e.g. A), enabling the user to click it more easily and more intuitively.

ACTUAL RESULTS

The 'Edit' popover button appears in the middle of the column, making it more difficult to be clicked by the user (see the screenshot).

If the mouse cursor is moved diagonally from the title of the entry to the button, there are chances that it disappears before the mouse reaches it. 

This also reproduces on the older XWiki versions.

summary: XSS using a JSX object
description:
It's possible to perform a XSS in JSX "on demand" or "on this document" which don't requires PR, just by creating a new JSX with edit right, and waiting for a PR user to execute it when accessing the page.
By doing so, we can request a PR user to create a page, or modify it, using any REST (or HTTP) request on the targeted wiki. 
Basically it allows privilege escalation.

label: Duplicate
summary: Adding a computed field property to an XWiki class updates all the pages having an object of that class with an empty revision
description:
How to reproduce:
* create a class on the wiki - the simplest is with an app within minutes
* create a couple of pages with an object of this class each
* go to the class - directly in the class editor it's simpler
* add a new property of type "computed field" to that class

Actual result:
* all the pages with objects of that class are marked as modified in their history, with a revision with message: "Migrated property [...] from class [...]"
* when diffed with previous version in history, this revision appears empty (no changes compared to previous version)

Expected result:
* there is no alteration or modification of the pages that contain objects of that class
* since the computed field properties are not supposed to have any value, should exist only at the level of the class and only for view (they're not even available for input in edit mode), they have no reason to leave any trace in the actual content document.

This is the same situation that is described by issue XWIKI-17633 , except that in this case it's about a *computed field* , so there shouldn't even be any change on the content.

Re-saving all content pages is bothering because it alters the timeline of the wiki, the document's last modification date metadata becomes irrelevant, wherever it appears. 
Document's last modification date is an important metadata for retrieving content - besides it being available all over the place in the index application it's also a standard facet of the search - see also XWIKI-18815 .

Very important: *there is no way to "fix" the updated pages if they were impacted by this issue* and bring them back to their previous modification date, other than restoring from a backup. Of course, if the issue is discovered late and there were already some changes on content in the meantime, restoring from backup is no longer an option.

Also, the class editor (the default complete one, not the one from AWM) is a bit tricky and adds a new property when the "add" button for the property is hit, not when hitting "save" at the bottom of the page, so even before hitting "save" on the page the damage is done.

{code:java}

The issue was reproduced also when performing an upgrade from XWiki 9.11.8 to 12.10.8 or 13.5; however, it didn't reproduce when upgrading from XWiki 10.11.11.

The issue can be very important for wikis with a large volume of content, since it alters last modification dates of documents.

The issue was initially discovered by [~lucaa].

comments.author: Ilie Andriuta
comments.body: Could it be possible that the source of the issue to be XWIKI-15812?

comments.author: Anca Luca
comments.body:
This issue is very worrying for XWiki installs / usages / applications for which the last modification date of the page is relevant, because this will actually update all pages with comments as if they had been updated at the upgrade time and will break the timeline of the wiki.

For example, some applications use the last modification date of the page as a modification date of the application data (e.g. file manager uses last modification date of a page as the last modification date of the file uploaded in the application).

There are a couple of panels in XWiki Standard flavor that display the "recent modifications", for the whole wiki or for the current user, all data of those panels will be impacted as well. 
The timeline of pages that can be obtained in the page index or in a page's child pages view when sorting descending by last modification date will also be broken by this update of history.

comments.author: Thomas Mortagne
comments.body:
bq. For example, some applications use the last modification date of the page as a modification date of the application data (e.g. file manager uses last modification date of a page as the last modification date of the file uploaded in the application).

This cannot be accurate for a page that accept comments, since any new comment will update the page date.

comments.author: Anca Luca
comments.body:
bq. This cannot be accurate for a page that accept comments, since any new comment will update the page date.

The fact that a _legitimate_ comment updates the last modified date of a document is more acceptable (even if sometimes may be considered inaccurate, for certain usecases) than having all pages updated massively with the date of the upgrade of the wiki, _without_ any real change in the page or in its comments or in any metadata at all.

label: Solved By
summary: Solr search discloses password hashes of all users
description:
*Steps to reproduce:*

Open {{<xwiki-host>/xwiki/bin/view/Main/Search?sort=score&sortOrder=desc&highlight=true&facet=true&r=1&f_type=OBJECT_PROPERTY&f_locale=en&f_locale=&text=propertyvalue%3Ahash*}} where {{<xwiki-host>}} is the URL of your XWiki installation.

*Expected result:*

No password hashes are displayed.

*Actual result:*

The password hashes of all users are displayed.

This allows efficient, offline password cracking attacks against in particular weak passwords. This shouldn't affect wikis that use external authentication (SSO) - however, in many cases, external authentication is used in a combination with local accounts and can be overridden.

From what I can see, this vulnerability has been introduced in XWIKI-8689 as the original Solr indexing code before that change had a check to not to index password properties.

summary: The Replay action gets stuck upon finding a conflict on a page, regardless of whether an answer is stored for that page or not
description:
*Steps to reproduce*
 # Login as Admin
 # Create 2 subwikis (subwiki1 and subwiki2)
 # Install an older version of an application in those subwikis (e.g. Blog App 9.13.1)
 # Go to one of subwikis (e.g. subwiki1) and modify a page on the respective application (for ex. on Blog App go to {{Blog.RssCode}} and empty it)
 # On the same subwiki (e.g. subwiki1) go to Administer Wiki > Extensions > Extensions
 # Search for the previously installed app (e.g. Blog)
 # Click 'Upgrade' > 'Continue'
 # When the page merge conflict is displayed (e.g. for modified page {{{}Blog.RssCode{}}}), select 'Keep the new version of the page'
 # Click 'Continue'
 # On the same subwiki (e.g. subwiki1) go to Administer Wiki > Extensions > History
 # Select the Blog App upgrade action (e.g. "Blog Application 9.13.2")
 # Click 'Export' and save the .XML file
 # Go to the other subwiki (e.g. subwiki2) and modify a page as well on the application (for ex. on Blog App go to {{Blog.BlogCode}} and empty it)
 # Go to Main Wiki > Administer Wiki > Extensions > History
 # Import the previously saved .XML file at Step 12
 # Check the box for the upgrade action
 # Click 'Replay' button
 # Fill the name of the subwiki not yet upgraded (e.g. subwiki2)
 # Click 'Continue' > 'Start' buttons

*Expected results*

* The replay of the application upgrade is finished successfully on the other subwiki (e.g. subwiki2).
* A question is asked to the user by the replay action for question Blog.BlogCode for subwiki2.

*Actual results*

The upgrade process is stuck (an endless spinning wheel displayed) at line:
{code:java}
Conflict between [@@ -1,1209 +1,0 @@] and [@@ -1,1209 +1,1209 @@]{code}
The issue was reproduced initially by [~lucaa].

comments.author: Anca Luca
comments.body:
so, the image  !Conflict_Stuck_Replay.png|thumbnail! actually shows a conflict on Blog.BlogCode, which is not the page with an answered conflict. Blog.RssCode is the page with the answered conflict.
However, I think it doesn't really matter on which page the conflict is, it always gets stuck on a conflict, regardless of whether it's on a page that's supposed to be answered in the history file or a page that is new. I am testing now all combinations and will update the ticket.

comments.author: Anca Luca
comments.body: indeed, on 14.4.3 it doesn't matter on which page the conflict is, whether it's an answered page or a new page, the replay process gets stuck on the conflict, and, for the case when it's an unanswered page, no question is shown to the user.

comments.author: Anca Luca
comments.body:
I tested on 14.4.3 and 11.10.1 and it also reproduces, the same.

On version 10.11.9 it works fine, as expected in the description above:
* Blog.RssCode is overwritten with the new version of the page from 9.13.2 with no question asked
* a question is asked to the user for Blog.BlogCode.

Thus, this issue is a regression as it used to work in the past.

comments.author: Anca Luca
comments.body: This looks a lot like issue XWIKI-19727 which also talks about a question of a replay job not being shown on the UI.

comments.author: Simon Urli
comments.body:
So the root cause of the issue seems to be XCOMMONS-1688. AFAICS the question is properly triggered during the InstallJob performed as part of the replay. But this InstallJob does not have the ReplayJob as parent, so the question is not asked to the parent, and since the UI is checking the status of the ReplayJob it never knows that a question has to be displayed. 

I will check a bit more XCOMMONS-1688, an easy fix seems to properly set the parent job when starting the child job in ReplayJob#replay but I'm not 100% sure about the side effects.

comments.author: Simon Urli
comments.body:
bq. an easy fix seems to properly set the parent job when starting the child job in ReplayJob#replay

ok not easy at all actually since there's no setter for AbstractJobStatus#parentJobStatus

comments.author: Simon Urli
comments.body:
So the root cause of the issue is this change:  https://github.com/xwiki/xwiki-commons/commit/f90c110b6fbe214f709ed74c188ac8e2994e577b#diff-e88373810031d08a81640e8ea098647d30a60e410908d669ce0bdb4f841c034fR67

Since the ReplayJob forces the child job to have their own context, when they start and the status is created, there's no parent job that can be found from the context (as part of this call: https://github.com/xwiki/xwiki-commons/blob/xwiki-commons-14.10.14/xwiki-commons-core/xwiki-commons-job/xwiki-commons-job-api/src/main/java/org/xwiki/job/AbstractJob.java#L379 and https://github.com/xwiki/xwiki-commons/blob/xwiki-commons-14.10.14/xwiki-commons-core/xwiki-commons-job/xwiki-commons-job-default/src/main/java/org/xwiki/job/internal/DefaultJobContext.java#L61)

So at this point I have the feeling that best for this specific UC would be to introduced a setter for AbstractJobStatus#parentJobStatus and use it as I mentioned previously in ReplayJob#replay.

comments.author: Charpentier Lucas
comments.body:
At least two ways to solve this issue:
- Add a [aria-labbeledby|https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Attributes/aria-labelledby] attribute to the image and reference the label next to it
- Add an "alt" attribute with an appropriate value to the image.

The second one can be useful if it makes sense to want a tooltip on this picture (title).

label: Solved By
summary: Copy-pasting content with images from a page in view mode to a page in wysiwyg edit mode adds images from attachments as external URL images
description:
Steps to reproduce:
* create a page A in your wiki
* edit the page and add a paragraph and an image
* save and view
* open another page B in your wiki, in edit mode
* copy the paragraph + image from page A in view mode
* paste this into the wysiwyg editor of page B
* save
* page B now looks exactly like page A

Expected result:
* page B also has the image of page A as an attachment

Actual result:
* the image on page B is added as an external URL image, pointing to the attachments of page A but not as a wiki reference but as an external URL
* thus, page A doesn't have any knowledge that there are some other pages on the wiki referring its attachments
** if page A is moved or deleted, the image on page B will be broken


Note that this is different from issue XWIKI-15350 in the fact that that issue is talking about copying between 2 open editors while this issue is about copying between a page in view mode and a page in edit mode.
The behaviour of XWIKI-15350 is actually "good" in the sense that it allows the editor to realize that something is not exactly as it should about their copy-paste, and maybe re-upload the image on page B. In the usecase of this issue it looks like it's all fine and the job was done as expected.

label: Solved By
summary: Open Redirect vulnerability discovered in the latest XWiki platform
description:
Hello XWiki team,

I discovered an open redirect vulnerability in the XWiki platform in the xredirect parameter.

*PoC*:

 If a victim goes to the following url: [https://xwiki/bin/login/XWiki/XWikiLogin?xredirect=//veryevilwebsite.evil] they will be redirected to https://veryevilwebsite.evil

This is because the exact value of the xredirect param ("//veryevilwebsite.evil") is sent to the Location header. 

*Recommended Fix*:

Consider removing every forward and backward slash except for one in the xredirect param as this will inform the browser the path is relative to the site and not an absolute one. 

 

Thanks,

comments.author: Simon Urli
comments.body: [~yibelo] thanks for reporting this. This issue has already been reported and we're working on it on XWIKI-19994. I gave you access to this ticket too so that you can follow up the fix.

comments.author: Paulos Mesfin
comments.body:
Hi @Michael and @Simon,

 

I wanted to add that modern browsers will parse http:example.com as an absolute URL and go to example.com from meta or Location headers. XWiki parses that as a relative URL so this opens a different path to open redirect. This also affects the xredirect path but utilizes : instead of // like my initial report. These tiny browser url parsing features cause mayhem everywhere. It makes sense to track these two as separate vectors and tackle them. Let me know if that's how you'd like to proceed. I'll also go check the fix for the // are good.

comments.author: Michael Hamann
comments.body: [~yibelo] Your comment on this closed issue hasn't been noticed until now, unfortunately. I confirm that while the issue with // has been fixed (though I'm not sure I agree with the [fix|https://github.com/xwiki/xwiki-platform/commit/e4f7f68e93cb08c25632c126356d218abf192d1e] to just drop support for such URLs entirely) but the issue with http:example.com still exists - thank you for reporting that one. Do you want to create a new issue for it or shall we just re-open this issue?

comments.author: Michael Hamann
comments.body: I've re-opened this issue as parts of it haven't been addressed yet, in particular in combination with the pattern {{http:example.com.}}

comments.author: Michael Hamann
comments.body: Also, XWiki seems vulnerable to the pattern [described by Sonar|https://www.sonarsource.com/blog/security-implications-of-url-parsing-differentials/]. For example, when your wiki runs on localhost, {noformat}http://example.com\@localhost{noformat} redirects to {{https://example.com/@localhost}} even though {{example.com}} is not trusted. I'm adding this here as we should address all of these issues at the same time when implementing XWIKI-20549.

summary: Cannot insert an image in WYSIWYG mode with the new image dialog after upgrading XWiki
description:
Steps to reproduce:

* Take a clean XWiki *13.10.5* (or any older version that ships with CKEditor Integration *1.61* or below, which doesn't have the new image dialog)
* Open _Wiki Administration > Editing > WYSIWYG Editor_ and check the list of "Disabled Plugins": the 'xwiki-image' plugin is not disabled (you can search for it when opening the drop down); moreover, there's no 'xwiki-image-old' plugin
* Save the configuration (no need to change anything, but the result is the same if you change)
* Open the _Extension Manager_ administration section, search for the CKEditor Integration extension and upgrade it to version *1.62* (or any newer version); 1.62 is the version when the new image dialog was introduced, see CKEDITOR-436
** Alternatively, you can get the same result by upgrading XWiki to 14.3-rc-1+ / 13.10.6+, i.e. any version that has CKEditor Integration 1.62+ (see XWIKI-19643)
* Clear the browser cache
* Go back to _Wiki Administration > Editing > WYSIWYG Editor_ and check again the list of "Disabled Plugins"; the 'xwiki-image' plugin *is still not disabled*, but if you search for 'xwiki-image' in the drop down you'll now see both 'xwiki-image' and 'xwiki-image-old'; this means the new image dialog is enabled
* Edit a wiki page with the WYSIWYG editor to see that the new image dialog is enabled (even though it's experimental)
** From CKEditor's toolbar, click Image
** Select an image from the Document Tree or Upload an image
** Click Select > Insert => the image is not inserted and there is a JavaScript error in the console
* If you go back to _Wiki Administration > Editing > WYSIWYG Editor_ and disable the 'xwiki-image' plugin (and save) then you get the old (working) image dialog

In browser's JS console, there are the following errors:

This issue was reproduced also in XWiki 13.10.8, but not reproduced in XWiki 14.6 or 14.4.2.

comments.author: Vincent Massol
comments.body:
Note: This issue is not blocker not labelled as regression because the new image plugin is not activate by default and our documentation at https://extensions.xwiki.org/xwiki/bin/view/Extension/CKEditor%20Integration/Features/#HImageAttachments says:

bq. The new image dialog is unstable on 13.x and it is not advised to activate in in production. If it happens to be activated following an upgrade, it must be deactivated.

comments.author: Marius Dumitru Florea
comments.body:
There are two problems:

* a bug in the new image dialog that prevented the image from being inserted; I think this was fixed in the latest versions of CKEditor Integration
* the fact that the new image dialog gets enabled "automatically" if:
** CKEditor Integration is upgraded from 1.61 or older (where the new image dialog didn't exist) to 1.62+ (where the new image dialog is available)
** the user has custom CKEditor configuration saved before the upgrade

The second problem is a "generic" configuration problem that happens when:
* there is configuration property whose value is a *list*, and it has a default value (e.g. [foo, bar])
* the user sets the property value (overwriting the default, e.g. [foo])
* the default value changes between versions (e.g. [foo, test])
* the user upgrades and his custom value is (still) overwriting the (new) default value

comments.author: Vincent Massol
comments.body: one idea for the second problem would be to do something similar to what we imagined for the macro categories in the future, i.e. something like:  {{+color, -family}} (i.e. store the diff with default, instead of the whole overriding value).

comments.author: Marius Dumitru Florea
comments.body:
[~mleduc] I'm on Linux (Ubuntu 20.04) and I can't reproduce. Could you please tell us the steps to reproduce? Do you reproduce when exporting any wiki page? Does the problem persist after a restart or when you try again on the same page? I'm asking because the error you got comes from the headless Chrome browser. Here's what I think happened in your case:

* we ask Chrome to open the PDF print preview page
* we ask Chrome to evaluate a script in order to determine if the page is ready (fully loaded); this script is *asynchronous*, so its execution may take some time
* somehow before the page ready script execution ends Chrome navigates to a different page (or reloads the current page), which destroys the execution context associated with the page ready script leading to "Execution context was destroyed" error.

I can't tell why Chrome navigates to a different page while the page ready script is running. You should open http://localhost:9222/json and "inspect" the tab that was used for the failed PDF export by opening:

{noformat}
http://localhost:9222/devtools/inspector.html?ws=localhost:9222/devtools/page/<id>
{noformat}

comments.author: Marius Dumitru Florea
comments.body: Actually I managed to reproduce this when exporting the home page. I'm investigating.

comments.author: Marius Dumitru Florea
comments.body:
The problem is that by default the home page displays a *tour* which reloads the home page (changes the window location) if the current URL doesn't match the URL specified in the first tour step. Even if the user has closed the tour in their own browser, this state is saved using *local storage*, so the headless Chrome browser used for PDF printing won't preserve the state and thus still get the tour on the home page. Of course, the URL used for printing targets the home page but it doesn't match the URL from the first tour step (different action, view vs. export, and different query string).

This shows that:
* we need a way to *disable the tour* per request / page load (i.e. when performing the PDF export)
* the generated PDF file may sometimes look different than what the user sees in view mode because some parts of the view mode are controlled by *local storage* (there's no usage on \{{localStorage}} in XWiki platform but extensions may use it)

* a page with JavaScript code that changes the window location on page load (like in the case of the tour, but the main search page does this also) can't be exported as PDF on the server side

summary: Random missing page from the cache but present in the database
description:
How to reproduce:
* it is not clear how this happens, the state just occurs from time to time on the wiki
* all the places where it was observed it was on farms with subwikis - but it could also happen in single wiki mode
* it was observed for user pages, group pages, server descriptor pages - this list is not complete.

When it happens, the defect is that there is one page (document) of the wiki that appears to not exist: navigating to the URL of that page / document displays "This page does not exist". No recent action was taken on that document or anything, it looks as it has just "disappeared" .
However, in other places the page is listed as existing: e.g. in livetables or elsewhere.
In the database, the document exists in the xwikidoc table.

Clearing the xwiki cache using the admin tools extension (or restarting the wiki) fixes it, the document is displayed correctly as existing.

Thus, the cause seems to be a wrong information about the existance of the document that is stored in the cache .

A lot of the times, these missing documents have impacts on evaluating rights on various resources, so they will be noticed, functionally, as a rights problem.

summary: Default email notification template should use a translated application name
description:
Right now the default notification email template uses an untranslated descriptor application name when sending notifications. 
However the documentation in https://extensions.xwiki.org/xwiki/bin/view/Extension/Notifications%20API/#HRecordableEventDescriptor advise to use a translation key for the application name, and that's what we do in general for custom events. 
We also call the localization script service to render the application name in the notification settings macro, so it makes sense to do the same in the email notification template.

summary: Autowatch is broken if all scope notification filters are removed
description:
Reproduction steps:
  - Create a new user: by default, it should have the automatic page watching set to "Every time I make a major modifications", and the pages notifications should not be enabled
  - Login with that new user and create a new page
  - Check in notification settings that a new custom filter has been created for that page
  - Remove this filter
  - Create a new page, or perform any edition 

Expected results:
  - all major edition should result to new scope notification filters being created

Obtained results:
  - no new filter is created, the whole wiki is watched so user receive notifications for any changes

comments.author: Simon Urli
comments.body:
This bug directly depends on XWIKI-19070 the problem is that a filter is created if the page is not already watched or if the event types are not yet enabled (in https://github.com/xwiki/xwiki-platform/blob/xwiki-platform-14.4/xwiki-platform-core/xwiki-platform-notifications/xwiki-platform-notifications-filters/xwiki-platform-notifications-filters-watch/src/main/java/org/xwiki/notifications/filters/watch/internal/DefaultWatchedEntitiesManager.java#L143). 
The problem is that when a first filter is created, the event types (pages event types) are automatically enabled. And when no scope notification filter is created, the whole wiki is considered watched. So no new filter can be created in such case.

comments.author: Manuel Leduc
comments.body: Since XWIKI-18397 and XWIKI-15460 remove notification filter preference, they might lead to the notification filter preference of a given user to become empty.

comments.author: Anca Luca
comments.body:
bq. Since XWIKI-18397 and XWIKI-15460 remove notification filter preference, they might lead to the notification filter preference of a given user to become empty.

I think this is fundamentally yet another argument in favor of XWIKI-19070 , since the impact will be even bigger on the notifications that the user receives: they may, all of a sudden, start receiving notifications for the whole farm (if everything that they were watching was deleted).

Actually, only XWIKI-15460. I don't see what kind of functional impact XWIKI-18397 has...

comments.author: Anca Luca
comments.body: Added a link to XWIKI-17540 which is also describing incomprehensible behaviour between the event switches and the autowatch: these 2 issues should be looked at together when fixed, to choose a solution that is coherent and handles both.

label: Solved By
summary: The JavaScript API to interact with a Live Data instance is not accessible
description:
The JavaScript API to interact with a Live Data instance is defined by {{Logic.js}}. This API is exposed in two ways:

* [{{liveData.js}}|https://github.com/xwiki/xwiki-platform/blob/xwiki-platform-14.2/xwiki-platform-core/xwiki-platform-livedata/xwiki-platform-livedata-war/src/main/webapp/resources/uicomponents/widgets/liveData.js#L115] saves a reference in the data of the root element, using the 'livedata' key
* calling [{{Logic(element)}}|https://github.com/xwiki/xwiki-platform/blob/xwiki-platform-14.2/xwiki-platform-core/xwiki-platform-livedata/xwiki-platform-livedata-webjar/src/main/webjar/Logic.js#L67] (actually {{init}}) returns the API associated with the given element (if the live data widget was already created)

In both cases you need to have access to the root element that is enhanced by the live data widget. The problem is that this element is replaced / detached so you can't access it anymore after the live data is created.. See XWIKI-19634 also.

We need to:
* either don't remove the root element (i.e. make it wrap the Vue.js component)
* or expose the Logic API on the root of the Vue.js component

comments.author: Michael Hamann
comments.body: I faced the same issue when researching options for getting the current filter and sorting values for exporting the Live Data and I [found|https://stackoverflow.com/questions/37507934/access-to-component-by-dom-element] that you can actually access the Vue.js component using {{element.\_\_vue\_\_}}, where {{element}} is the DOM node of the component. This means that, for example, {{document.getElementById('wikis').\_\_vue\_\_.logic}} actually gives you access to the logic instance of the {{wikis}} Live Data. I don't think we should consider this an official API, but it might be a workaround.

label: Solved By
summary: Privilege escalation via style sheet skin extensions with just edit rights
description:
It is possible with a full CSS style sheet (but not a simple style-attribute) to exfiltrate any attribute value with one request per character with the help of a specially crafted server, see [Better Exfiltration via HTML Injection|https://d0nut.medium.com/better-exfiltration-via-html-injection-31c72a2dae8b]. A particular technique detailed there using {{@import}}-directives allows to execute this attack in a single request by the victim. This can be used to exfiltrate the token used as CSRF protection of the current user. As XWiki allows basically everything with just a get request, the external server that has the CSRF token can then directly deliver  (via a style sheet that is requested later via {{@import}}) a specially crafted URL as background image URL that changes, e.g., a user profile to grant more privileges or just saves a page with a groovy script. The attacker just requires edit privileges for creating a style sheet extension that is used on the current page.

This is basically the same as XWIKI-9119 just for style sheet extensions and with an attack scenario that is more complex as it requires a special external server that is reachable from the browser of the victim.

To protect against such attacks, we should consider either requiring programming rights (which might be a bit extreme) or at least prevent this attack by disallowing {{@import}}-directives unless the user has programming rights. There are also other attack vectors, though, and in particular if the attacker can modify the style sheet extension while the victim with programming rights is accessing them several times while a token is valid (currently as long as XWiki hasn't been restarted) this is not going to prevent anything (see the linked article for details how the attack is executed).

Note that as long as XWIKI-10009 hasn't been fixed and the attacker has script rights, no complex token extraction techniques must be used but the token can be obtained using {{$\{services.csrf.getToken()}}} and directly used in the URL of a background image.

The affects version is tentative and taken from XWIKI-9119. I haven't actually tried reproducing this in real as setting up the test server would require some time but I do not see why it shouldn't be feasible given that the blog article linked above demonstrated the attack, the token is readily available in an attribute of the top-level HTML element and there is no special filtering of CSS as far as I'm aware.

I'm giving this a medium priority for now as the attack seems far more complex than other issues and I think we should first fix XWIKI-10009 as it seems far more obvious to exploit.

comments.author: Simon Urli
comments.body: Adding a script right check for ssx as part of the fix for XWIKI-9119, I believe it's enough to fix this.

label: Solved By
summary: The size of the delete and move click targets in the attachments tab is too small
description: The click targets of the delete and rename action in the attachments tab below the document are just 22x22 pixels large which is quite small and fails WCAG 2.1 Success Criterion [2.5.5 Target Size|https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG21/#target-size] (Level AAA, see also [Understanding Success Criterion 2.5.5: Target Size|https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Understanding/target-size.html] that requires that target sizes are at least 44 by 44 CSS pixels. While both actions have a confirmation step so both can be easily undone, I think they are really too small and we should take this fail seriously.

comments.author: Marius Dumitru Florea
comments.body:
None of our buttons have 44px height and I don't think you can find many examples on the web were buttons have that height:

* CKEditor toolbar buttons have 30px height
* JIRA buttons have 30px height
* Bootstrap buttons have 34px height
* Google Mail toolbar buttons have 40px height (with icons 20px by 20px) while the in-page buttons have 36px height

I'm not saying the click targets for the attachment actions are big enough, but for me 44px height is too much. I'm fine to make the clickable area larger up to 34px, to match the buttons height (not necessarily using a larger icon but using padding around the icon as Google Mail does).

Note that you can activate from the user profile the accessibility mode and we could make the click targets larger (44px height) when this mode is activated.

comments.author: Marius Dumitru Florea
comments.body:
BTW, the permalink click targets from [https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG21/#target-size] is only 7px by 17px:

 !w3c-permalink.png|thumbnail! 

and I find the permalink action at the end of the heading line to be very similar to the delete and rename actions at the end of the attachment line. Sure, in case of the permalink the action is available also in the table of contents, but it's highly unpractical to find the link there.

comments.author: Michael Hamann
comments.body:
I do not insist on the 44px. For me personally, the problem here is really the fact that these two different actions are very close together and it is thus very easy to click on one while wanting to click the other.

Regarding your example, the guidelines explicitly mention that this does not apply if the action is available in another place of the page. Further, as there is no other action close by, if you miss the click target, simply nothing happens and you can try again immediately. On the other hand, in our case you first need to either close the delete confirmation dialog (thereby making sure not to click on the wrong button) or going back to the previous page if you clicked on the move action.

Note that this problem can be solved by implementing XWIKI-13454 using Live Data which would add text to the actions (which imho greatly improves the usability as in particular the move icon is not obvious at all) and thus make them larger automatically.

To sum up there is different problems:
  1. commentfield.vm is called twice when Clicking on "Add comment" with guest user and Captcha is enabled (only once when Captcha is disabled)
  2. commentfield.vm performs a hack to insert a property in CommentClass, by using BaseCollection#put and then removes it using BaseCollection#removeField here the systematic double call creates a race condition, but the same race condition can probably occurs if many people are trying to comment
  3. the reason why we have a race condition is because BaseCollection is not thread safe, and more specifically BaseCollection#fields is not a ConcurrentHashMap 

So we should be able to fix the recurring behaviour displayed by this ticket just by fixing 1. Now, it will still happen from time to time, and we should definitely remove the hack exposed in 2. Finally 3 should be done as an improvment for avoiding all those issues in the future.

summary: Notifications Watched page/space/wiki switches display as "on" in the case of an exclusive filter unless _all_ events are excluded
description:
By default in XWiki, if a user doesn't watch anything, it's considered that they watch everything. A side-effect of this is that the watch switches are on everywhere.
The usecase I'm trying to implement is to disable this, and not send any notification to a user as long as they haven't suscribed (watched) any page.

Steps to reproduce:
* I'm activating the "page" events
* I'm creating an exclusive filter for the whole wiki, for all the events except for "Mentions".
** including the mention events in the excluded events here would prevent me from receiving mention notifications, since this is how targetable events work (they're impacted by exclusion filters) and this not what I want
 !image-2021-10-20-23-43-43-561.png|thumbnail! 

Expected result:
* the switches are off on the pages so that I can actually start watching pages to receive notifications for them
!image-2021-10-20-23-44-34-139.png|thumbnail! 

Actual result:
* the switches are still on for pages, I cannot subscribe to any page, they all appear as watched even if I don't receive any notification
 !image-2021-10-20-23-45-52-362.png|thumbnail! 

I think this behaviour was introduced by XWIKI-17787 .

This issue reproduces exactly the same for a globally set exclusion filter.

The default that everything is watched unless explicitly excluded along with this issue that make exclusions very difficult to use.


See also https://forum.xwiki.org/t/clarify-the-behaviour-of-notification-watch-switches/7471/14 where I mentioned this usecase.

comments.author: Anca Luca
comments.body: [~surli] could you please confirm that this behaviour is a regression introduced by XWIKI-17787 ?

comments.author: Simon Urli
comments.body: So it's kind of a regression of XWIKI-17787. Now by following your steps and watching afterwards the whole wiki you'd have created a contradictory filter: your previous exclusive filter would have remained in place because it doesn't concern all events, and a new inclusive filter would have been created for all events. See on this topic XWIKI-17788. So the issue here is that XWIKI-17787 should have been fixed with a watched button representing a middle state. I'm planning to do that for XWIKI-20648 and close this one as solved by it.

Related to XWIKI-20314

Reproduction steps
 * make the wiki multi-lingual
 * add a new supported language (e.g., fr)
 * make the new language the default language
 * Create a new page or edit an existent one (which is not the sandbox page. It works curiously as expected when using the sandbox)
 * Make a screenshot using any tools (tested with default windows tool, win + maj +s, print keybutton, greenshot)
 * Paste it into the editor
 * Save the page

Expected:

The attachment name should be random.

Actual result:

The attachment name is __fileCreatedFromDataURI__.png

 

I'm up to provide any info needed.

Thank you,

label: Cannot Reproduce
summary: Notifications not properly rendering main wiki URLs in subwikis
description:
I do not have the possiblity to build a test-deployment. But steps to reproduce should be: # Install Domain-based Wiki # Login as Admin # Create a subwiki # Login as an user (e.g. U1) # Go to Notifications > Settings # Set all Pages Notifications to ON # Go to the subwiki created previously # Click on Notifications bell and turn 'Watch this wiki' toggle to ON # Login as Admin # Create, update and comment a page on the subwiki # Create, update and comment a page as well on Main Wiki # Login as U1 # Go to subwiki and observe the notifications list ---- Since the upgrade from version 13.10 to 14.6 and now also with 14.10, we have a problem with the display of notifications in subwikis. !https://forum.xwiki.org/uploads/default/original/2X/3/3a908009ff8dfd6706502b492a3f9eb4497dfabe.png!   Viewed as HTML one can see, that both, link to the wiki page and the profile, are generated as relative URLs. (Example below reflects the image part.) {code:java}
bearbeitet von Johannes Wielsch
vor 1 Woche
{code}

comments.author: Ilie Andriuta
comments.body:
Hi! I've tested on XWiki 14.10.1 and 14.10.2 (Jetty/HSQLDB) and I couldn't reproduce the issue.

I've followed these steps:
 - Added 2 custom domains in {{/etc/hosts}} file (my system is Windows 11): {{elijahxwiki.com}} for Main Wiki and {{elijahsubwiki.com}} for the subwiki
 - Unzipped a new instance of XWiki 14.10.2
 - Edited {{{}xwiki.cfg{}}}, uncommented and set {{xwiki.virtual.usepath=0}}
 - Started and accessed the instance with {{elijahxwiki.com}}
 - Logged in as Admin
 - Created a subwiki with Alias: {{elijahsubwiki.com}}
 - Created an user U1 on Main Wiki
 - Logged in with U1, went to Notification Settings and set Pages Notifications toggles to ON
 - Went to subwiki, clicked on Notifications bell and made sure 'Watch this wiki' toggle is ON
 - Logged in as Admin
 - Created, updated and commented a page ({{{}Sub1{}}}) on subwiki
 - Created, updated and commented a page ({{{}M1{}}}) on Main Wiki
 - Went to subwiki, logged in as the user U1
 - Checked the notifications list

I've included 2 screenshots from inspecting Admin's avatar image and the link to {{M1}} page created on Main Wiki ({{{}elijahxwiki.com{}}}), both viewed from U1's Notifications list on subwiki ({{{}elijahsubwiki.com{}}}). The links do not appear to be relative.

I've also tested on path based wiki and I couldn't reproduce the issue.

On this screen, it's not clear to me why the SubThemeTemplate is grayed out and why I cannot check it. I can still click on the checkbox next to the SubThemeClass, which seems to select the SubThemeTemplate :

 !image-2022-12-09-23-32-20-188.png|thumbnail!

comments.author: Simon Urli
comments.body:
bq. On this screen, it's not clear to me why the SubThemeTemplate is grayed out and why I cannot check it.

What's grayed out is the list of pages that uses xobjects of the defined xclass. It's an informative view to allow you open and check the xpages that will be impacted by the xclass deletion. And you cannot act on them since once the xclass is removed, the xobject will be automatically invalidated on those. 

Now I've not been able to reproduce the bug on a fresh wiki using 14.4.6 (or 14.10) following those steps:
  - Creating a page TestXClass containing a String property
  - Creating a page TestXObject containing an xobject of type TestXClass with some test value
  - Deleting TestXClass page

I performed the test twice first by checking manually the box, and second by clicking on "Select all": each time the page gets deleted. Note that I tested both times on firefox.

comments.author: Ilie Andriuta
comments.body: I also tested on a XWiki 14.4.7 instance and on a 14.10 (Edge 108) and couldn't reproduce either. In my case, the same test page contained both the xclass and the xobject.

label: Cannot Reproduce
summary: xwiki-image: Image upload to non-English pages has bad results
description:
In the new image dialog xwiki-image, uploading images on non-English pages does not work as desired (you need to upload an image via the dialog to reproduce this). If you do this, the image is uploaded but linked incorrectly. In source code or wiki mode, there is an additional `attach:` in the path in all language versions, which is rendered as `attach%3A` in the image src path in HTML on non-English pages. The image is displayed during the editing process but not displayed in view mode after saving the page (broken link to source).

On English pages this does not happen, the image is displayed properly both in edit and view mode.

label: Cannot Reproduce
summary: Reset Password link affected by browser session cache or cookies
description:
Hi. When a user tries the Forgot your password option, they receive the reset password email, but if they tried the option in the past and opened an old reset password link in the same browser session, when they access just once the new reset password link they get the message:

Wrong parameters! Another link was already sent or this one was already accessed!

The current workarounds are to open the reset password link:
- in a different browser or
- in a private/incognito session or
- only after deleting the browser's cookies and cache

comments.author: Marius Dumitru Florea
comments.body:
[~iandriuta] the JavaScript stacktrace you pasted is definitely not from XWiki 13.10.3. The Applications panel JSX doesn't use RequireJS on 13.10.3 as you can see [https://github.com/xwiki/xwiki-platform/blob/xwiki-platform-13.10.3/xwiki-platform-core/xwiki-platform-panels/xwiki-platform-panels-ui/src/main/resources/Panels/Applications.xml] (simply search for "require"). The usage of RequireJS was introduced by XWIKI-19429 in 14.1RC1 with [https://github.com/xwiki/xwiki-platform/commit/0775036399624a3d42e6d3f03a56aebc9d6c6464#diff-b754c82d7c5f3a1bf15667a2bc29786e6bdcde755ffbddafa60f8ec289a413b8R412] .

Please try again on a clean XWiki 13.10.3 and make sure to clean your browser's cache. Something was not right on your setup.

comments.author: Ilie Andriuta
comments.body: Indeed, it seems to be the browser's cache fault, as after clearing the cache I don't seem to reproduce the issue anymore.

label: Cannot Reproduce
summary: Wiki toolbar breaks the html macro when using displayEdit

comments.author: Simon Urli
comments.body:
A workaround for this bug is to actually escape the wiki macros provided by the toolbar:
{noformat}
#set ($editor = $doc.displayEdit($contentField, '', $messageObj))
  ## This is a hack to ensure that the wiki editor does not break the html macro. 
  $!editor.replace('{{', '&;#123;&;#123;')
{noformat}

PR created related to this: https://github.com/xwiki/xwiki-platform/pull/1794 closed because of disagreement on it with [~mflorea]. 
Full discussion about it on: https://matrix.to/#/!ikPtGZaGWtyblizzlR:matrix.xwiki.com/$1646822934736ZnalG:matrix.xwiki.com?via=matrix.org&via=matrix.xwiki.com&via=caubin.fr

To sum up, I consider this is a bug since I think we should be able to use {{displayEdit}} API in a wiki page either inside or outside an html macro, but without needing to perform further escaping. Moreover, this one might be hard to spot since we don't necessarily control which editor will be displayed: in my case I missed the bug because I was always using WYSIWYG editor where this escaping is not needed. 

According to the previous discussion, [~mflorea] considers this is not a bug since the dev should control what they use in a wiki page, and perform the appropriate escaping. So according to him, the workaround I pasted is not a hack and is the accurate solution.

comments.author: Marius Dumitru Florea
comments.body:
To be clear, I think you are focusing too much on wiki editor tool bar while the problem is more generic:

* *any* xproperty displayer can produce {{\{\{/html\}\}}} or other wiki syntax in their HTML output
* users can write their own *custom* xproperty displayers, overwriting the default ones
* we cannot expect or assume that users writing custom xproperty displayers will encode the "{{" characters
* since we don't always control the output of the xproperty displayers (we can only assume it's HTML, but not necessarily valid) it means the output is *not safe* (not to be trusted) and thus we have to be careful when injecting that output into a wiki page. It's the same as with the translation messages: we don't always control them (the user can overwrite) so we need to make sure that when we display a translation message it doesn't break the context (HTML, wiki syntax, JSON, whatever).

Fixing the wiki editor toolbar doesn't fix the problem. It fixes only one instance of the problem. In order to fix the problem we need to:
* either ask developers to perform escaping when injecting the output of a custom xproperty displayer (i.e. the hack you mentioned)
* or modify {{displayEdit()}} (and possibly other {{display*}} methods) to escape *automatically* the '{{' characters in the output of a custom xproperty displayer

comments.author: Simon Urli
comments.body:
bq. or modify displayEdit() (and possibly other display* methods) to escape automatically the '{{' characters in the output of a custom xproperty displayer

I do think that's the direction to go yes.

label: Cannot Reproduce
summary: The wording of the (empty) option of the list filters of livedata is misleading
description:
Livedata tables have a new filtering option for list columns, that livetables didn't have: the possibility to display only the rows having _no value_ for the property of that column (in livetables it was only possible to filter tables having a given value for the column).

This option is presented in the livedata filters dropdowns as "(empty)". 

 !Selection_103.png|thumbnail! 

However, since empty is also a verb, it's not clear that that option will filter rows having no value, I understood it as "clearing the filter", "emptying the filter value". 
Even more so that the livedata filter does not have the "All" option anymore, that the livetable had, which cleared the filter, and that the new "(empty)" filter is positioned _exactly_ where the "all" filter used to be in the livetable, at the top of the list.
Maybe this issue should be about restoring the "All" option.

comments.author: Eduard Moraru
comments.body: I was able to reproduce the issue locally (jetty-hsqldb) after installing the antivirus application which intercepts {{DocumentUpdatingEvent}}s in order to detect and scan attachments that were added or modified: https://github.com/xwikisas/application-antivirus/blob/400935f/application-antivirus-api/src/main/java/com/xwiki/antivirus/internal/AttachmentUploadedEventListener.java#L94

comments.author: Eduard Moraru
comments.body:
The *problem* seems to be the following:
* The Antivirus application is calling {{doc.getOriginalDocument().getAttachmentDiff(originalDoc, doc, context)}} (https://github.com/xwikisas/application-antivirus/blob/400935f/application-antivirus-api/src/main/java/com/xwiki/antivirus/internal/AttachmentUploadedEventListener.java#L187-L189) which seems to be a method that has *unexpected and undocumented side-effects of altering the XWikiDocument object on which it was called*.
* Before the call, the original document's (deleted) attachment has the field {{content}} set to {{null}}. When the Antivirus application is not installed (i.e. when a listener does not call {{getAttachmentDiff}} during the {{DocumentUpdatingEvent}}), the {{content}} field stays {{null}} and then {{XWikiDocument.retrieveDeletedAttachment}} successfully manages to reload the attachment from the attachment archive (recycle bin) because {{XWikiAttachment.getContentInputStream(context)}} first tries to reload and only then it tries to read the content's input stream. That input stream ends up being {{null}} due to {{XWikiAttachment.getContentInputStream()}} returning {{null}}.
* However, when the {{content}} field is not {{null}} (like in the usecase exemplified by the Antivirus application), {{XWikiAttachment.getContentInputStream(context)}} directly tries to load that content from the {{FilesystemAttachmentContent}}, which results in a {{FileNotFoundException}}, since the attachment's file has just been dele

label: Invalid
summary: Never tagged pages are not listed in query results when searching for pages without a specific tag
description:
When running a query to find pages in a particular space *_without_* a specific tag, the query only returns pages that have been tagged at some point, even if the tags have been deleted.  Pages that have never had any tag set on them are not in the results, even though they don't have the specific tag from the query.

For example, if I run the following query in a velocity script:
{code:java}
#set ($spaceReferenceString = "Development")
  #set ($query = $services.query.xwql("select doc.title, doc.fullName from Document doc, doc.object(XWiki.TagClass) tag  where ('someTag' not member of tag.tags) and (doc.space like :space or doc.space like ':space.%') order by doc.fullName asc"))
  #set ($query = $query.bindValue('space').literal("${spaceReferenceString}.").anyChars().query())
  #set ($results = $query.execute()) {code}
The results will include:
 * Pages with tag(s) that are not 'someTag'
 * Pages that previously had a tag, but they have been deleted (no tags currently)

The results will NOT include:
 * Pages that have never had a tag

Logically, pages that have never been tagged should also be included in the group of pages that do not include 'someTag'.

summary: Page lock warning when resolving a version conflict by selecting "Reload the editor (discard changes)"
description:
*Steps to reproduce*
 # Login as Admin
 # Go to a page
 # Open the same page in a different browser (or an incognito window) and login with the user (U1) there
 # With Admin, edit the page in-place (insert e.g. 'edit1')
 # Click 'Save'
 # With U1, on the incognito window (force edit the page if the case), add some text e.g. 'edit2' on the same line
 # Click 'Save'
 # Go back to the browser where Admin is logged in and type a word (e.g. 'edit3') in the same line
 # Click 'Save'
 # On the Version Conflict box, select 'Reload the editor (Discard changes)'
 # Click 'Save'

*Expected results*

The page lock is not displayed and the content is saved with the last modification saved by the user (e.g. 'edit2').

*Actual results*

A page lock is displayed that the page is currently locked by U1. However, the content is saved as expected.

The lock could be reproduced also on XWiki 14.10.6 and 14.10.7, but could not be reproduced on XWiki 14.10.5.

comments.author: Simon Urli
comments.body:
So I believe the change of behaviour is related to XWIKI-20690 now I'm not fully sure we should consider this as a regression or even as a bug: in the scenario described by Ilie, the second user is still performing edition and Admin has lost their lock. So I've the feeling that it does make sense to require forcing the lock again to reload the editor there. 
Now, maybe the bug is more that we don't have this behaviour for other editors: the same scenario when using the wiki editor doesn't require to force the lock. So for me we should probably fix the inconsistency between editors, but I'm not sure I would fix this behaviour even if it's a side effect of some other changes and was unexpected. 

TL;DR: it's a feature, not a bug.

comments.author: Thomas Mortagne
comments.body: I find 2G for the whole system quite low, honestly. There are a lot of optimizations on XWiki SAS Cloud instances, and they are allocated much less than 1024M AFAIK.

comments.author: Simon H.-R.
comments.body:
If it helps, I am now running a well running "very small" instance (4-5 concurrent users) based on the Debian package as outlined in the issue description.
 It currently uses a bit over 3 GB of memory - the 2 GHz vCPUs are rather "bored". I use the following JAVA_OPTS.

{{JAVA_OPTS="-Djava.awt.headless=true -Djava.security.egd=[file:/dev/./urandom|file:///dev/urandom] -Xms800m -Xmx1024m"}}

So my impression is that 2 CPUs and 4 GB of memory would suffice for a small all-in-one installation.

label: Invalid
summary: Watch page switches are set off when editing mail settings
description:
For some reason the watch page switches are automatically turned off in some conditions when using the email settings in administration. 

Reproduction steps:
  - On a fresh  jetty/hsqldb demo
  - Login with Admin user and go in administration
  - Create a new user and put an email address to it
  - Add this new user to the XWikiAdmin group
  - Login with this new user
  - Click on the bell to see the watch page switches: they should all be on
  - Go back in administration and in Mail sending section
  - Fill information for "Email address to send from", "Email server port", "Send wait time"
  - Save changes
  - Click on the bell to see the  watch page switches

Expected result:
  - switches are still on

Obtained result:
  - switches are off, even going to another page still display them off

Note that for some reason, this behaviour does not reproduce when using the Admin user itself.

description:
STEPS TO REPRODUCE
 # Login as Admin
 # Create a page and upload some attachments on it
 # Create an user (e.g. U1)
 # Login as Admin
 # Disable the user's account (from Administration or from the user's profile page)
 # Login with the user U1
 # In the upper right search box, search for the previously uploaded attachments' names
 # Click on the suggestions

EXPECTED RESULTS

As the user's account is currently disabled, no search suggestions are displayed when searching.

ACTUAL RESULTS

The uploaded attachments are displayed as suggestions and they can be accessed/viewed by the disabled users, or downloaded.

label: Invalid
summary: UIX will cache content even if "cached" property is disabled when "Asynchronous rendering" is enabled
description:
When a UIX "Asynchronous rendering" property is set to true, no matter what the value of its "cached" property is, the UIX content will be cached.

Reproducible on a fresh 13.10 instance.

Step to reproduce:
- Create a new page "Sandbox.testUIX"
- add code containing user info, like:
{code:java}
{{velocity}}
crtUserDoc.fullName: $crtUserDoc.fullName
hasAdmin: $hasAdmin
{{/velocity}}{code}
- set "Asynchronous rendering" to "Yes"
- set "Cached" to "No"
- set any "Extension Point ID" so that you can see the content, like "org.xwiki.platform.template.contentFooter"
- set "Extension Scope" to "Global"

To see what's going on:
- Open any page where you can see the specified extension point ("Sandbox.testUIX" should do it): it should correctly display your current user info, as it is the first time it loads.

Then:
- Open the same tab in another browser / session / firefox container, using any another user. The data shown by the UIX is still your first user info, because the result has been cached, even though the "cached" property was set to "No"

comments.author: Thomas Mortagne
comments.body:
bq. using any another user

You don't seem to enable "User" in "Context elements" property. This means that the context user is never given in input of your code. So it's not that the result is cached, it's just always the same (because the context user is always the same).

label: Invalid
summary: XSS via Unvalidated File Upload
description:
The application does not perform proper checks on images uploaded via the WYSIWYG editor when creating new pages.

 

Malicious users are able to modify new images uploads, changing the file name and extension type to _.html_ allowing the execution of potentially malicious code for any user visiting the relevant image URL.

 

NOTE: I was unable to reproduce this using Tomcat and MySQL via the latest Docker image when testing.

 

+Recommendations+

Perform validation on the file extension before file uploads are persisted in the DB. Create a case-insensitive check against an allow-list of safe file types and reject any uploads that do not meet this.

 

+Version info+

!image-2021-06-21-01-06-51-957.png!

 

+Steps to Reproduce+
 # Download the Jetty/HSQLDB trial/test instance from: [https://www.xwiki.org/xwiki/bin/view/Download/DownloadVersion/?projectVersion=12.10.8]
 # Unzip and run start.sh
 # Log in as an admin.
 # Create a new application.
 # After creating application, click 'ADD NEW ENTRY' and save name in modal.
 # Click 'edit'/pencil icon next to new entry.
 # Click '+ Create' 
 # Add a title and select 'Blank Page' from the 'TYPE' options and select 'Create'.
 # Upoad a local image.
 # Intercept the image upload with proxy software such as Burp Suite and make the following changes:
 ## Change 'filename' to _xss.html._
 ## Change 'Content-Type' to _text/plain._
 ## Remove the image data and replace with the below Javascript:

{code:java}
<script>alert(document.location)</script>{code}

 # Forward or replay the request. Make a note of the _url_ field in the server response.
 # Copy and paste the url field value into a browser. Code should execute.

 

+POST Request+

comments.author: Marius Dumitru Florea
comments.body: [~3therk1ll] note that there is a way to force the *download* of an attachment rather than displaying / executing it in-line in the browser. See https://www.xwiki.org/xwiki/bin/view/Documentation/AdminGuide/Attachments#HSecurity . {{text/html}} is black-listed by default. The issue here, if I understood correctly, is that you managed to force the content type to {{text/plain}} for an HTML file upload, and {{text/plain}} is white-listed so displayed in-line by default. Then maybe the issue is that we trust the content type provided by the uploader, although I'm a bit surprised because I know we're using Tika to determine the content type and it should properly detect HTML, but maybe we call Tika only when the content type is not specified on the upload request. To be checked.

comments.author: Richard Curteis
comments.body:
[~mflorea], regarding the Content-Type, I think a strict allow-list of allowed types in line with the intended content for upload coupled checks on the file extension being uploaded and denying anything that could be rendered by the DOM as executable code, JS/HTML. As this is an image upload maybe a case-insensitive allow-list of image file extensions?

Does that make sense?

comments.author: Richard Curteis
comments.body: [~mflorea] is there any timeline for a fix on this? I would like to disclose

comments.author: Richard Curteis
comments.body: Hi guys, it's been three months since submission. Please can you let me know if this is something you intend to fix. I will wait until 9th November to disclose, three months from your first response.

comments.author: Thomas Mortagne
comments.body:
bq. maybe we call Tika only when the content type is not specified on the upload request

Yes.

What is actually really surprising to me is that the browser execute as HTML something which has text/plain as mime type (the download action send back the attachment mime type with the content). It does not make much sense.

comments.author: Thomas Mortagne
comments.body:
So I just tried that with Firefox and Chrome and those definitely do *not* execute the attachment content if the mime type is text/plain (feels like you did not really changed the mime type as much as you think with your proxy, you can see the mime XWiki actually received in the database in the table xwikiattachment).

It does execute it when the mime type is "text/html" which you can reproduce simply by attaching the html file to a page and clicking on it. But that's something you can do only with a user who has programming right, with another user you get a file download and not an inlined html content.

So all in all I cannot reproduce what you describe here.

comments.author: Thomas Mortagne
comments.body:
bq. feels like you did not really changed the mime type as much as you think with your proxy

On that front actually I checked the code and the request mime type is simply not taken into account at all. That's why your proxy does not have any effect, the stored mime type is text/html. So I think you were just fooled by the fact that users with programming right are allowed to upload unsafe attachments.

A new captcha login is shown.

* Install https://extensions.xwiki.org/xwiki/bin/view/Extension/Numbered%20Content/Numbered%20Headings%20Application/ToC%20Macro/
* Create a wiki page with this content
{noformat}
{{toc/}}

= Header 1 =

== Header 1.1 ==

(% data-xwiki-rendering-protected="true" %)
=== Header without number ===

=== Header 1.1.1 ===

(% data-numbered-headings-start="10" style="--numbered-headings-start: 9;" %)
== Header 1.10 ==
{noformat}
* Activate numbered headings for this page
* Export the page to PDF with the table of contents option checked

Expected result: the PDF table of contents shows the heading numbers, as it happens when the table of contents macro is called within the exported content.

Actual result: the heading numbers are shown only when the table of contents macro is called within the exported content.

comments.author: Vincent Massol
comments.body:
So after several days of investigations, here's the explanation:
 * It's a problem related to Tomcat 9 (works fine with Tomcat 8 which explains why it was seen as a regression). It also works fine with Jetty.
 * In Tomcat 9, tomcat performs an internal mapping very early when a request is received (at the level of [Coyote|https://github.com/apache/tomcat/blob/7d3d359aaa8b7fe9463a73915340a347ad5e4614/java/org/apache/catalina/connector/CoyoteAdapter.java#L354]), and it uses the Request URI to map to the Servlet to handle it. Since the URI is {{/upload/...}}, there's no mapping in {{web.xml}} that matches it and it's thus mapped to the Default Servlet (which isn't configured to parse multipart requests (which is used in XWiki since when uploading we do a POST and pass the {{form_token}} in the body, thus the request is multipart). 
* This early mapping happens before any filter declared in XWiki has executed (and thus before the URLRewriteFilter has executed, and thus before that filter adds the {{/bin/}} prefix to the request URI...). Note that this wasn't the case in Tomcat 8 or older versions. 

There are several solutions: 
* Solution 1: Force Tomcat to perform a multipart parsing by setting {{allowCasualMultipartParsing="true"}} in {{context.xml}} (you can set this in the XWiki webapp in {{META-INF/context.xml}}). 
** There could be bad side effects since tomcat is using the default servlet in this case and not our action servlet... it seems to work but who knows wha

comments.author: slauriere
comments.body:
I'm reopening this issue since it seems it's actually an XWiki issue if I understand correctly. Indeed the [Servlet 3.0 specification|https://download.oracle.com/otn-pub/jcp/servlet-3.0-fr-oth-JSpec/servlet-3_0-final-spec.pdf] mentions in section "3.2 File Upload":
{quote}If a request is of type multipart/form-data and if the servlet handling the request is annotated using the @MultipartConfig as defined in Section 8.1.5, the HttpServletRequest can make available the various parts of the multipart request via the methods getParts and getPart.
{quote}
And as a complement, [Tomcat9 documentation|https://tomcat.apache.org/tomcat-9.0-doc/config/context.html] about the attribute {{allowCasualMultipartParsing}} mentions:
{quote}Set this attribute to true if Tomcat should automatically parse multipart/form-data request bodies when HttpServletRequest.getPart* or HttpServletRequest.getParameter* is called, even when the target servlet isn't marked with the @MultipartConfig annotation. Note that any setting other than false causes Tomcat to behave in a way that is not technically spec-compliant.
{quote}
Beside being not spec-compliant, setting {{allowCasualMultipartParsing}} to {{true}} raises an issue described in XWIKI-20796.

[~AndreeaChirica] you cannot expect the shrinked image to have the same quality as the original image (with the original size). Some information is lost during the resize. Now, the resize can happen on the client (browser) or on the server. The browser usually does a better job. See https://www.xwiki.org/xwiki/bin/view/FAQ/How%20to%20improve%20the%20avatar%20image%20quality . You can either:

* prevent the server side resize (through the {{rendering.imageDimensionsIncludedInImageURL}} configuration or by resizing from CSS rather than from CKEditor)
* increase the quality of the server side resize, through configuration

This issue is a Won't Fix for me.

I honestly don't see enough differences between the original and the resized version to worth a BUG issue like it was the case for XWIKI-7623, you cannot really expect a perfect resize.

label: Won't Fix
summary: Debian packages install full PostgreSQL server
description:
I've just installed XWiki from Debian packages and found that it depends on and thus installs a full PostgreSQL server. However, I already have an external database server setup for other projects, so I don't need (or better: want) another full server running on the wiki host.

Since the packages also don't ask for database parameters, I needed to manually dump the database after installation, import it on my database server and change the hibernate configuration.

It would be better if the package had specified alternatives for the database connection (like, for example: "postgresql|libpq" and in addition use Debian's package configuration system to ask for database parameters during package installation.

comments.author: Vincent Massol
comments.body:
There are actually 2 problems:

1) We need a DTD defined.
2) The following syntaxes are not working anymore:

{code}
  <Call name="prependSystemClass">
    <Arg>-javax.mail.</Arg>
  </Call>
  <Call name="prependServerClass">
    <Arg>javax.mail.</Arg>
  </Call>
{code}

And

{code}
         <Get name="systemClasspathPattern">
           <Call name="add"><Arg>-javax.mail.</Arg></Call>
         </Get>
         <Get name="serverClasspathPattern">
           <Call name="add"><Arg>javax.mail.</Arg></Call>
         </Get>
{code}

comments.author: Vincent Massol
comments.body:
The working version of jetty-web.xml is:

{code}
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE Configure PUBLIC "-//Jetty//Configure//EN" "https://www.eclipse.org/jetty/configure_10_0.dtd">

<Configure class="org.eclipse.jetty.webapp.WebAppContext">
...

  <!-- Tell jetty that javax.mail should be something that is invisible to the user, but if it's provided inside the
       webapp use that instead (this is the case for XWiki). This is needed for work around issue
       https://github.com/appropriate/docker-jetty/issues/108. Note that we don't have this problem in the XWiki
       Standalone packaging since we create a custom distribution of Jetty and we don't include the Jetty "mail"

comments.author: Anca Luca
comments.body:
I would probably need to investigate a little more, but IIRC there is no flow between the page frame (header, footer, margins left and right) and the page content in the (fop) document model - which means that the different areas are fixed boxes with fixed positions on the page and the content of one does not "push" the content of other to make room, unlike on the web.
I think this is also what would happen when manually preparing a file in an office suite, when used properly to define page headers / footers / content.

So either we 
* enlarge page header _all the time_ , to fit the maximum of characters that may endup in there (255 + 3 + 255)
* compute the size of the page header per printed pdf (instead of having a frame that applies to all the pdf exports), in order to dinamically set the sizes of the page elements based on the specificities of one page.

comments.author: slauriere
comments.body: As far as I understand, the header does not push indeed the following elements, and the page body starts at a position controlled vertically by variable {{page-margin-top}} in the default {{xhtml2fo.xsl}}, which is set to {{<xsl:param name="page-margin-top">1in</xsl:param>}}. Increasing this value all the time would mean a high {{page-margin-top}}, even higher now that page titles can be longer than 255 characters. Instead, this variable could be computed dynamically indeed. The header text is computed in {{pdfheader.vm}}, not sure yet how to adjust {{page-margin-top}} depending on the output of {{pdfheader.vm}} using XSL syntax (in case this is the way to go).

comments.author: Anca Luca
comments.body:
Another option that I can think of now is to not display the full page name if the name is too long. Keep the current header as is in terms of size, but make sure that the overlapping cannot happen: don't display text, hide it, etc.

What I see for now is that there is some room on the right and on the left of the title... I'm wondering why that space is there and whether the actual text would fit on 2 lines if we would not have that margin.

So, [~slauriere], if you want to try continue on this issue, you can try to look at what's the source of those margins...

comments.author: Marius Dumitru Florea

comments.author: Marius Dumitru Florea
comments.body: Tables are not responsive by default. You need to follow [https://www.xwiki.org/xwiki/bin/view/Documentation/DevGuide/FrontendResources/SpecialCSSClasses/#HClassesfortheresponsiveness] to make them responsive. I fixed the "Compare XWiki to Confluence" page on xwiki.org. You can see my changes here https://www.xwiki.org/xwiki/bin/view/Compare/XWiki-vs-Confluence/?viewer=changes&rev1=2.3&rev2=3.1& .

comments.author: [I'm so sorry!]White Cloud
comments.body: [~mflorea] Thank you so much.May the Xwiki team produce a table that can be adapted to the content or width of the page?

comments.author: Marius Dumitru Florea
comments.body:
[~Damoebai] there's no magic solution. Tables don't scale like images or text. A table requires a minimum amount of horizontal space and if the screen is smaller than that then you get an overflow and horizontal scroll bar. The minimum width required is directly proportional with the number of columns. The bigger the number of columns the bigger the minimum width required. That's why one solution, but which can't be applied automatically ATM, is to reduce the number of columns to 2 on small screens: one column for headers (repeated) and one column for values (you basically end up having key / value rows).

In any case, you need to state your problem more clearly. Best is to provide an example table for which you have the problem.

comments.author: Simon Urli
comments.body:
That's actually a change of behaviour linked to the pre-filtering of Notifications (XWIKI-17439). While with post-filtering the Notification settings are used after the notifications are sent, to filter them for the display, with the pre-filtering the Notifications settings are used when the notifications are sent so even if you change the settings afterwards it doesn't have any impact on the notifications you receive. [~tmortagne] said it clearly in the Release Notes for 12.5 (https://www.xwiki.org/xwiki/bin/view/ReleaseNotes/Data/XWiki/12.5/#HMiscellaneous):
bq. events are associated with users right when they happen and the association is stored, this means changing your notification configuration won't have any impact on already stored user notifications

So IMO we should close it as wontfix.
